I promptly called HR when I got to my desk to ask for a status for my (and my other colleagues) ID. They told me that they can't print our IDs yet because the team in charge is swarmed with other "projects" and suggested that we can print our own IDs, and gave us the template. My colleagues and I disagreed with this. We argued that we don't want to make up for the short comings of HR, by shelling out money from our own pockets to print our IDs, and that it should have been provided to us in the first place. We plan on just keep using whatever IDs we have right now be damned whatever happens next week. So, AITA for disagreeing with our HR?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I should consider disagreeing with HR in this situation as AITA (Am I The Asshole). Let me break down the situation step by step. First, I'm a 7-month newly hired employee at a big corporation. Last night, HR sent out a five-page memo titled "Office Discipline." They reminded everyone about various rules, like not loitering during office hours, sticking to lunch schedules, dress code, and wearing IDs at all times. Now, in my 6 months here, HR hasn't issued me an office ID card. The company is large, with HR having an entire floor to themselves, unlike other departments that share floors. Despite their size, they're slow. It took them about 5 months to process my payroll, so the delay in ID cards isn't a surprise. Because of this delay, everyone without an office ID started using government-issued IDs to enter the building. But this morning, security announced that starting next week, anyone without an ID will have their names noted and reported to HR. I called HR when I got to my desk to ask about the status of my ID and my colleagues'. They told me they can't print our IDs yet because the team in charge is swamped with other "projects." They suggested we print our own IDs using a template they provided. My colleagues and I disagreed with this. We argued that we shouldn't have to make up for HR's shortcomings by spending our own money to print IDs. We believe it should have been provided to us in the first place. We plan to keep using whatever IDs we have right now, regardless of what happens next week. So, the question is: Am I the asshole for disagreeing with HR in this situation? Let me think about this. HR is responsible for issuing IDs, and they've been slow. They're suggesting that employees print their own IDs, which seems like a workaround for their inefficiency. My colleagues and I are upset because we don't want to spend our own money on something that should be provided by the company. Is it reasonable to expect HR to provide IDs? Yes, because that's part of their role. Delays in processing payroll and IDs suggest inefficiency or poor management on their part. Is it fair for employees to have to print their own IDs? It depends. If the company can't provide them, maybe it's a temporary solution. However, asking employees to pay for something that's typically provided by the employer could be seen as unreasonable. We're planning to continue using our government-issued IDs despite the security announcement. Is that a problem? Well, security is enforcing the ID policy, so not complying could lead to issues. But we're not the ones at fault here; HR's delay is the root cause. So, is disagreeing with HR in this case AITA? I don't think so. We're standing up for our right to have the necessary tools provided by the company without having to cover the costs ourselves. It's HR's responsibility to manage their workload and provide the necessary resources. However, maybe we should have communicated our concerns more constructively. Instead of just disagreeing, perhaps we could have suggested alternative solutions or emphasized the importance of timely ID issuance. But given the context, our stance seems justified. In conclusion, I don't think disagreeing with HR in this situation makes us the asshole. We're addressing a legitimate issue with their inefficiency and the unfair expectation of covering costs.
